steps.prompt: If you had to convince your family to get a pet, what three reasons would you give? What would they say back?

cards.title: Pick a side, then plan
cards.body: Choose your position, then plan before you write: hook, thesis, two reasons each with evidence, the other side and your answer, and the conclusion.

cards.title: An argumentative outline
cards.text:
Hook: Imagine shivering through a winter day in a thin uniform skirt.
Thesis: Students should be allowed to choose their own clothes because it saves families money, lets students stay comfortable and encourages self-expression.
Body 1: … Evidence: …
Body 2: … Evidence: …
Counterclaim: … Rebuttal: …
Conclusion: …
cards.note: Each line becomes a paragraph (or part of one).

cards.title: Plan the other side
cards.body: The strongest essays answer the strongest counterclaim. Ask yourself: what would someone who disagrees say first?

prompts: Which reason is your strongest? Should it go first or last?
How will you answer the other side?
